results.value: Qualitative: the blue-wing gas at 1.9" S of S is most consistent with dense gas in the blue lobe of the known southern bipolar outflow (Sakamoto+2014; Michiyama+2018), not an unrelated cloud. results.value: Blue window (2300-2575): HCN flux in the box 0.485+-0.067 (Xb4d) vs 0.27+-0.11 (Xb4b) Jy km/s, i.e. 55+-25% recovered at 0.25"; HCO+ 0.26+-0.09 vs 0.22+-0.14; Xb4b resolves the lobe into 20-40 connected >3 sigma regions (peak 0.131 Jy/beam km/s HCN, S/N 33; 0.096 HCO+, S/N 11) with only 0.8 arcsec2 (HCN) above 3 sigma: the lobe is clumpy/diffuse at <0.25" (<50 pc) scale rather than a single compact cloud.

interpretation: Line inventory (corrected): besides HCN and HCO+ (J=2-1,3-2,4-3) and CS 7-6, CH3OH is detected (Band 5 165 GHz Q-branch J=1-3 at 27 sigma; 2(0)-1(-1) E at 254.015 GHz at 10 sigma), SO 5(4)-4(3) (Band 5, 8 sigma) is detected, HOC+ is tentative; everything else is a limit, blended or an edge artefact. CH3OH is cold/subthermal (Q-branch J>=4 and Eu>45 K lines absent; LTE Trot~9 K, but LTE and RADEX fits are poor) and extended: the Xb4d (0.9") CH3OH flux is only ~55% of the 9"-beam value, and in Xb4d it peaks on the Bridge and a W clump, not on the N and S nuclei (CH3OH/HCO+ 0.05 there vs <0.015 at the nuclei) - a shock/low-excitation tracer signature that agrees qualitatively with Harada+2018. The extended disk is defined (Xb55 HCO+ 2-1 S/N>5 at r>8", HCN/HCO+(2-1)=0.51) but is not detected in the 3-2/4-3 data with the available sensitivity/zero-level. The southern blue-shifted component 1.9" south of S is statistically solid (7-12 sigma after null calibration, 0 null peaks above 8 sigma in 583 beams), has no red counterpart, is not a PSF-sidelobe copy of S, and has HCN/HCO+(3-2)~1.8 versus 0.4 at S; it is a separate broad component at ~2560-2650 km/s. The N and S nuclei are separable in Xb4b, Xb4d, Xb4f, Xb47 (not in Band 5). The opacity test (H13CN) can only give HCN/H13CN>7-9 (conditional on the CO-wing model). Raw HCN/HCO+ (3-2) peak ratios (N 0.6-1.0, S 0.4-0.5) are preliminary and not beam matched across OUS (Q1). Q1 (rev. 2): At matched 1.05" the northern nucleus has HCN/HCO+ 3-2 = 0.83+-0.04 and the southern (AGN) nucleus 0.40+-0.02 (N/S = 2.0-2.1, constant over the line core, insensitive to the velocity window to <=2.5% and to Xb4b vs Xb4d); the AGN has the lowest ratio, i.e. no HCN enhancement at the AGN (as Harada+2018). Blended 6.5"/10" aperture ratios hide this (N/S 1.1-1.2), but deblending the native-beam Band 7 4-3 map with the 1" templates recovers N/S = 1.9+-0.5 (N 0.47, S 0.25) and CS 7-6 tracks HCO+ (N=S) not HCN; at 2-1 (9" beam) the N-S pair is not separable (contrast 1-3, template-limited). The ladders (3-2/2-1, 4-3/3-2: HCN 0.35/0.39 (N), HCO+ 0.43/0.48) are strongly sub-thermal and the same at N and S within 14% (HCN 4-3/3-2 lower at S, 1.8 sigma): a quick RADEX grid gives n(H2) <~ 1e5 cm-3 and Tkin >~ 30 K at N, and requires N(HCN)/N(HCO+) >= 3 at both nuclei; since the ladders do not differ, the factor-2 N/S HCN/HCO+ contrast must come mainly from the HCN/HCO+ abundance (or HCN column/opacity) rather than density or temperature (equal-X disfavoured at ~2 sigma only). The disk 2-1 HCN/HCO+ is 0.47-0.50, 15-25% below the nuclei at the same beam; its 3-2 deficit is fully consistent with missing short spacings in Xb4f for a 13-14" scale structure (B_min = 8.7 m assumed), so no excitation difference of the disk can be claimed from HCO+; the HCN 3-2 deficit is larger than recovery alone explains but depends on the zero level. The Soutflow blue-wing HCN/HCO+ is 1.2-1.8 depending on estimator (candidate, single position, HCO+ wing 5-7 sigma). Resolution forces an 'active region versus disk' comparison at J=2-1 and for the disk, but not at J=3-2 and 4-3, where N and S are distinguishable. Q3 (outflow): dense gas (HCN and HCO+ 3-2) is detected in the blue wing 1.9" (370 pc) south of the S nucleus (HCN 12.6 sigma, HCO+ 5 sigma), in the location, direction and sense of the blue lobe of the edge-on southern bipolar outflow (Sakamoto+2014; Michiyama+2018), with a red counterpart toward OF-Red between the nuclei and no wing at N (pole-on outflow, <1-2% of core). The lobe shows a blueshift gradient perpendicular to the E-W rotation gradient and an HCN/HCO+ 3-2 ratio rising from 0.6 at lobe core velocities to >=2 at -300..-400 km/s (1.7+-0.35 in the wing), ~4x S and ~2x N, while the red lobe is nuclear-like (1.0+-0.2). This matches Michiyama+2018 (dense-gas fraction rising with velocity) and resembles the high HCN/HCO+ shells of Nishimura+2024 (shock chemistry), but the data do not prove the origin; RADEX (tentative) points to an HCN/HCO+ column or abundance ratio >~10 rather than density. M_dense ~6e6 Msun (factor 2-3) in the blue wing. caveats: Peak-pixel intensities use different native beams per OUS; no cross-OUS ratio in this item is beam matched (Q1/Q6).

Systemic velocity 2780 km/s is a single adopted value; nuclear peak velocities differ by ~100 km/s at 0.25" (N 2811-2817, S 2710), so +-350 km/s windows are not centred on each nucleus; the HCN/HCO+ integrals use the same fixed window for both lines.

Line identifications rest on Splatalogue CDMS/JPL rest frequencies at v=2780 km/s; HOC+, SO 4_5-3_4 and both unidentified features need independent confirmation (e.g. matching J transitions at matched beam).
The Band-5 cubes do not separate N, S, Bridge (13% leakage at the nuclear separation, single HCO+ 2-1 peak pixel).
Empirical noise comes from emission-free pixels at 6-11" (primary-beam-corrected noise there is 1.2-1.6x the central value), which makes limits conservative by up to ~1.5x.
Xb4b nuclear emission is clumpy: peak-pixel values depend on the exact pixel chosen (search radius 1"); spectra are non-Gaussian (double-horned), Gaussian FWHM are indicative only.
No source of data for line-free-channel continuum from cubes exists (cubes are continuum-subtracted); the contamination check relies on mfs vs cont images, which have 1-2 sigma noise.
The 'aperture' (1.5" radius) rows of the line table use statistical noise only (no empirical null).
The conversion to K km/s uses the Rayleigh-Jeans formula with the beam of each cube; distance 40 Mpc is only used for pc sizes.

CH3OH LTE/RADEX fits have chi2/dof ~9-11: the numbers Trot=9 K and n>=1e7 are formal; the robust statement is 'Q-branch J>=4 absent: low excitation'. Baseline ripple of ~0.2 K km/s is visible in Band 5 (J=5 at -4 sigma).
Local-velocity matching (not 2780 km/s) is essential for identifications at S (2710-2740 km/s): at vsys the 251.66 feature would favour NS; at local velocity it clearly favours CH3OH.

The zero level of Xb4f/Xb55 moment-0 maps at r>8" is biased by about -0.5 / -1.3 Jy/b km/s (negative bowl, missing short spacings); disk fluxes are zero-level-corrected with the r=14-22" ring and carry >=0.3 Jy/b km/s systematic.

Soutflow position error is dominated by the assumed 10% beam pointing floor (0.10"), not by the fit (0.01-0.02"); wing definition relative to v_S=2722; comparison with the CO outflow geometry (Sakamoto+2014, Michiyama+2018) has not been made quantitatively.
H13CN limit conditional on the CO-wing family; log-quadratic/cubic wings can absorb a genuine H13CN signal.
Literature cross-check is from abstracts/summaries (Harada+2018, Sato+2022), not their tables.

Q1: ratio uncertainties are dominated by systematics (window truncation ~5%, absolute flux scale 10% per band); statistical errors are <=1% at the nuclei. Noise uses few line-free windows contaminated at times by weak lines (quietest quartile used), so faint-region limits are approximate.
Q1: regions use fixed nominal positions; the N ratio varies across its sub-clumps (IQR 0.05-0.09 at 1.05"), so a different aperture centre changes N by ~0.03-0.05.

Q1: the decline of HCN/HCO+ and the low 3-2/2-1, 4-3/3-2 ladder ratios at 10" mix Band 5, 6 and 7 data with different resolved-out fractions (Q6: Xb4f is the most complete Band 6 set); they should be treated as inputs to RADEX with 14% errors, not as evidence for a nuclear difference.

Q1: the Xb55 2-1 "disk" may include beam wings of the nuclei and NEclump; the ring zero level (-1.2 to -2.0 Jy/b km/s) is not present in line-free channels, so the sign of the correction is uncertain.

Q1b: the deblending assumes a uniform ratio inside each template component and that the 1" 3-2 template traces the same gas as the coarse line; chi2_r of the fits is 7-44 even with a 3% floor, so formal errors are meaningless and template systematics (a factor ~2 on N/S flux ratios at 2-1) dominate. Only the 4-3 N/S HCN/HCO+ contrast (1.9+-0.5) survives the injection test.

Q1b: the disk recovery model assumes B_min and a single Gaussian disk; the array identity is inferred from beam sizes (no uv information in the products). The zero-level (ring) correction of the disk maps changes the 3-2 ratio by a factor of 4, so disk 3-2 statements are limits.

Q1b: RADEX constraints come from 5 ratios and 4 parameters (1 dof), assume equal beam filling for all lines and a single (n, T) per region for HCN and HCO+; they bound n(H2) and X, not the absolute columns. The H13CN limit is conditional on the CO-wing model of p0001.

Q3: the Soutflow association with the southern outflow rests on position, a velocity gradient and the red counterpart, not on CO kinematics (no CO in these data); the HCO+ blue wing is 5 sigma (one of 22 line-free windows has an 11 sigma HCO+ peak from another line), the HCN wing is 12.6 sigma. Blending: CH2NH/CH3NH2/CH3OH near the HCN wing are limited at the nuclei to <=2% of the peak, but the outflow chemistry may differ (up to ~10-15% of the wing could be methylamine in the worst case). 3-2/1-0 ratios depend on Michiyama+2018 fluxes (30% errors, unknown zero velocity), on possible resolved-out 3-2 flux, and the dense-gas mass on alpha_HCN and r31 (factor >=2-3). HCN/HCO+ values in the lobe are 1.05" beam averages. The red lobe at OF-Red lies between N and S and cannot be assigned to one nucleus. The N outflow limits apply only to compact dense gas.
